messages.text: Alright, let’s start: operating contract is 14 TeV hadron collider, kick it off as suggested with a common readout module.

I’ll start an isolated common HCAL readout-module prototype, with 14 TeV pp collisions recorded as the operating contract. I’ll make the tile, SiPM, front-end functions, power and cooling interfaces explicit, and keep the remaining rate and lifetime assumptions visible.

I’m using the repository’s specialist workflow and the `acts-spack` skill for the prototype and native checks. The preflight found changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, so I’ll re-verify the installed runtime before building with it.

For the module design, I’ll keep the common tile board distinct from the carrier that collects power, data and cooling. That should let us study shared services without repeating the old per-cassette overhead.

The first candidate is a compact 6 × 6 board with 36 tiles and one H2GCROC-class front end. I’ll account for all 78 chip channels—72 ordinary plus six auxiliary—including the unused capacity. Two boards will share a carrier, cooling plate and service interface.

That favors a small reusable board for barrel and endcap packing. I’ll retain the 72-tile alternative in the comparison, since it would use the front end more efficiently.

The module now has a named SiPM reference with published package dimensions. The independent review caught a clearance issue at its maximum specified height; I’ve deepened the proposed recess before building the geometry.

The new material model also uses an explicit C8H8 polystyrene host. Optical yield and aging remain separate inputs to establish later.

The first geometry check passed: 72 physical tiles, all 72 sensitive IDs, 360 cell-position probes and zero overlaps. Navigation also follows both cooling bores continuously through the plate and frame.

The bandwidth screen shows a constraint to retain: the assumed payload uses 93.75% of the DAQ allocation at 750 kHz and exceeds it at 1 MHz. That is a budgeting result; it does not yet establish sustained readout performance.

The common module is built, and the native geometry and two saved Geant4 muon events pass. Review found that the smoke-test report needed stronger links to the actual simulation inputs; I’m fixing that provenance check and adding rejection tests before closing out the prototype.

The prototype now includes two 36-tile boards on a shared carrier, physical board gaps, cooling bores, service connections and continuous-power accounting. The rate screen also exposes a limit: under the current framing assumptions, 750 kHz uses 93.75% of DAQ capacity, while 1 MHz exceeds it. Sustained readout remains a required follow-up.

The final rerun passes: 44 module and provenance controls, 14 existing calorimeter regressions, 395 native physical parts, 72 unique sensitive IDs, zero reported overlaps, and two saved Geant4 muon events. Independent review also confirmed both checker fixes. I’m recording the reproducible evidence and remaining qualification work now.

The design, schematic and validation report are ready. Two findings guide the next step: the proposed copper plate dominates the carrier’s 3.02 kg mass, and the assumed readout has little margin at 750 kHz. Those need thermal and occupancy studies before repeating the module into larger HCAL assemblies.

Implemented the first [common HCAL module prototype]([redacted] including its schematic.

- Two identical **36-tile boards** share cooling, power and data services.
- Explicit SiPM/LED packages, PCBs, physical gaps, materials and channel identifiers.
- Continuous-operation budget: **5.94 W nominal**, **3.02 kg** for both boards and carrier.

[Validation passed]([redacted] 44 new controls, 14 existing regressions, native geometry with zero reported overlaps, and two saved Geant4 muon events. Independent review findings were corrected.

The first constraint is clear: assumed DAQ utilization reaches **93.75% at 750 kHz** and **125% at 1 MHz**. Occupancy, framing and queue simulation should therefore accompany the next thermal and optical studies.

**14 TeV is the confirmed operating contract.** Other operating values remain explicit planning assumptions. The design remains an isolated DRAFT prototype, with component and engineering qualification pending.
